title: SCAFFOLD: Stochastic Controlled Averaging for Federated Learning
layout_note: A parameter-space sketch: two clients' local SGD trajectories drawn as chains of dots diverging from a common start, the server's averaged point between them, the client optima and true optimum as square markers on the right, and a legend column at the far right.
grouping: No containers. Meaning is carried by marker colour and arrow colour, keyed in a right-hand legend column (client update, server update, SGD update, client drift, true opt., client opt.). Client 1's path runs up, client 2's down; labels sit at the ends of each path.
shapes_depth: Flat vector sketch: iterates are filled circles (dark grey start and server point, blue client iterates, pale grey intermediate averages); optima are small squares (blue true optimum, orange client optima) joined by a dashed line. Arrows are thin and colour-coded (blue client steps, green server steps, black drift); small white squares mark the centralised SGD reference steps. Bold italic math labels (x, y_1, x*_1).
proposed_highlight: No method is shown; the figure isolates the problem the paper fixes - the averaged server point lands away from the true optimum because client paths drift toward their own optima (orange squares).
lesson: Show heterogeneity as geometry: draw each client's local steps as a dot chain bending toward its own optimum marker and the server point as their average, so client drift is visible without a single equation.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF footer (Proceedings of the 37th ICML, PMLR 119, 2020). Annotation note (2026-11-15): concept sketch of client drift (the problem), not a method/architecture diagram.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.note: modality multi = the method is data-agnostic; the figure is a parameter-space sketch with no data

core.what: federated updates drawn as iterates in a 2-D parameter plane: from a dark start point x, blue client steps head toward client 1 and client 2, green server steps go to grey averages, and orange client optima x1*, x2* and a blue true optimum x* are placed as squares off to the right

relations.form: circles are iterates placed in parameter space; client optima and the true optimum are squares at their positions, with a dashed line joining x1* and x2*
two rounds unrolled left to right: x splits into y1 (up) and y2 (down), each client takes further blue steps along its own path, and the server node is drawn after the second round
green server-update arrows run from x and from the first-round iterates into grey midpoint circles between the two client paths, averaging them
vertical black 'client drift' arrows with small white 'SGD update' squares connect grey/server points with client points to mark how far each client wanders

channels.colour: arrow colour = update type (blue client, green server, black drift); node fill = role (dark x/server, blue client iterate, grey average); square fill = optimum type (orange client, blue true) - blue thus means both 'client' and 'true optimum'
channels.shape: circles = iterates, filled squares = optima, small white squares = SGD updates
channels.line: solid arrows = updates; one dashed line joins the two client optima
channels.frame: none; the legend is an unframed column at the right

quality.strengths: the method's problem (client drift) is drawn on the space it happens in, so the gap between averaged iterates and the true optimum is visible as distance; arrow colours are keyed
quality.weaknesses: blue codes both client iterates and the true optimum; the grey average nodes are not in the legend; the white 'SGD update' squares sitting on drift arrows are hard to decode; the optima are placed far right, away from the trajectories they explain

insights.structure: A parameter-space sketch with no containers: two clients' iterate chains diverge from a start point x (client 1 up, client 2 down), a dark 'server' point sits between them, optima are square markers to the right, and a legend column fills the far right.
insights.data: Iterates are filled circles (dark start and server, blue client iterates, pale grey intermediate averages), optima are squares (blue true optimum x*, orange client optima x1*, x2* joined by a dashed line), and small white squares mark centralised SGD steps.
insights.emphasis: No method is drawn; the problem is made visible as geometry — the server point lands off the true optimum because blue client chains bend toward their orange optima.
insights.flow: Reading is left to right from x along colour-coded thin arrows (blue client steps, green server steps, black vertical drift arrows), ending at the legend.
insights.avoid: Legend arrows are drawn as tiny vertical strokes that are hard to match to the thin diagonal arrows in the sketch; the grey intermediate circles are not keyed.

arrangement.units: one unframed vector sketch with labels placed at path ends
arrangement.inputs_as: a dark filled circle labelled x (starting parameters)
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; optima squares at the right stand for the objectives
